— France’s Directorate General of Armaments (DGA) launched a SyLEx (Système de Lancement d’Expériences) sounding rocket developed by ArianeGroup during the night of November 3–4, 2026, at the Biscarrosse test range. The rocket carried experiments supporting the development of the future M51.4 submarine-launched ballistic missile (SLBM).
The launch took place less than a month after an unarmed M51.3 missile was test-fired from the ballistic missile submarine Le Vigilant on October 6, 2026. That test also supported the M51.4 program, with ArianeGroup confirming that the missile carried additional experiments for the next version.
The DGA awarded ArianeGroup the contract to develop and produce the M51.4 on August 28, 2025. It will be the fourth version of France’s M51 SLBM, which forms the backbone of its sea-based nuclear deterrent.
The M51.4 is expected to enter service in the 2030s aboard the current Le Triomphant-class submarines and France’s future third-generation ballistic missile submarines.
According to the DGA, the new version will offer greater range and accuracy, along with improved capabilities to penetrate adversary missile defenses.

— The American company Shield AI has unveiled the first full-scale prototype of the X-BAT, a next-generation, AI-powered combat drone featuring stealth technology and vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) capabilities.
The X-BAT is a large jet-powered unmanned aircraft, comparable in size to a conventional fighter jet.
The first full-scale prototype has been designated X-BAT 001. It has a stated range of up to 3,700 km and a service ceiling of approximately 15 km. Its wingspan measures around 12 meters, making it wider than that of the F-16.
According to its developers, the X-BAT will be capable of engaging in air-to-air combat, striking ground targets, and conducting reconnaissance missions.
It will carry weapons in internal bays and on external hardpoints, while autonomous flight and mission control will be powered by Shield AI’s Hivemind AI system.
The U.S. Navy has allocated approximately $200 million toward the X-BAT’s development, with Shield AI committing an additional $200 million.
The first prototype is being sent to a test site in Kansas, where engine and VTOL system testing is scheduled to begin before the end of 2026.
